Morning. How was your weekend?
Quiet. I did not do very much on Saturday, to be honest. I caught up on sleep.
That counts. Did you go anywhere on Sunday?
I took my daughter to a museum nearby. It was completely crowded.
On a Sunday it always is. Was it worth it?
The queue was terrible and I did not enjoy the first hour. But she loved it, so yes.

Hi, it is me. Listen, I have to tell you about Saturday, because it did not go to plan at all. We booked a table for one o'clock at that place by the market. We arrived at five past one and the restaurant was closed. Closed on a Saturday. So we walked to the square instead, and it was so crowded that we gave up after ten minutes. In the end we bought bread and cheese and we sat in the park on our own for two hours, and honestly it was the best afternoon I had all month. Anyway, call me back. I want to hear what you did.

Last year I took eleven days off and I did not travel once. People kept asking me where I went, and the honest answer was nowhere. I stayed at home, I caught up on about forty things, and I finished two books I started in twenty twenty-four. The first three days were terrible. I felt guilty and I checked my email far too often. Then something changed. By the second week I stopped looking at the phone in the morning, I walked somewhere new every afternoon, and I ended up knowing my own neighbourhood better than I did after fifteen years of living in it. It was not a holiday. It turned out to be something better.
